messages.subject: nimble function compile error (simulate model)
parts:
Hello All,

I cannot seem to get this nimble function to compile, hoping an expert could take a look:

I am running simulations for an occupancy model (for evaluating model fit in this case), the function below takes a model, and input nodes then runs and outputs n simulations.  it also takes parameter point values or parameter distribution values (model output samples) and either sets the relevant simulation parameters to the point values, or to random draws of the distribution values. The un-compiled function runs and seems to work correctly,  but I keep getting the same error when I attempt to compile it.


function:

## notes:  simulate occupancy nimble model
## setup: input model and defined nodes
## run:
##    n =  n simulations
##   mod = vector of 3 logical vals for p, alpha, beta,  true include, false ignore
##   useDist = logical vector, True use distribution, false use point, for p, alpha, beta
##  p.point, alpha.point, beta.point = point values for for defined nodes
## p.dist, alpha.dist, beta.dist = model output distributions for defined nodes.
##
##  input nodes should include a point value, or distribution for simulations


n.simulateModel.occ.dist<-nimbleFunction(
  setup = function(model, nodes) {
    dependentNodes <- model$getDependencies(nodes, self = F, downstream = T)
  },
  run = function( n = double(),
                  mod = logical(nDim = 1, sizes = c(3)),
                  useDist = logical(nDim = 1, sizes = c(3)),
                  p.point = double(),
                  alpha.point = double(1),
                  beta.point = double(1),
                  p.dist = double(1),
                  alpha.dist = double(2),
                  beta.dist = double(2)
                  ){
    nObs <- length(model$y)
    sim <- matrix(type = 'integer', nrow = nObs, ncol = n)
  
    if(mod[1] == TRUE) {               ## set values for p
      if(useDist[1] == TRUE){          ## use an input distribution for  p
        p.index <- trunc(runif(n, 1, length(p.dist)))
        p.in <- numeric(length = n)
        for( i in 1:n){
          p.in[i] <- p.dist[p.index[i]]
        }
      }else{                           ## use a point value for p
        p.in <- rep(p.point, n)
      }
    }else{
    
    }
  
    if(mod[2] == TRUE){                 ## set simulation values for alphas
    
      if(useDist[2] == TRUE){                ## use a matrix of distributions to set alphas
        n.alpha <- length(alpha.dist[1,])
        n.dist <- length(alpha.dist[,1])
        alpha.in <- matrix(type = 'double', nrow = n, ncol = n.alpha)
        for(i in 1 : n.alpha){
          alpha.index <- trunc(runif(n, 1, n.dist))

          alpha.in[,i] <- alpha.dist[beta.index , i]
        }
      }else{                                             ## use point values to set betas
        n.alpha = length(alpha.point)
        alpha.in <- matrix(type = 'double', nrow = n, ncol = n.alpha)
        for(i in 1 : n.alpha){
          alpha.in[,i] <- rep(alpha.point[i], n)
        }
      }
    }else{
    
    }
  
    if(mod[3] == TRUE){                                   ## set simulation values for betas
   
      if(useDist[3] == TRUE){                             ## use a matrix of input distributions to set betas
        n.beta <- length(beta.dist[1,])
        n.dist <- length(beta.dist[,1])
        beta.in <- matrix(type = 'double', nrow = n, ncol = n.beta)
        for(i in 1 : n.beta){
          beta.index <- trunc(runif(n, 1, n.dist))

          beta.in[,i] <- beta.dist[beta.index,i]

        }
      }else{                                               ## us point values to set betas
        n.beta = length(beta.point)
        beta.in <- matrix(type = 'double', nrow = n, ncol = n.beta)
        for(i in 1 : n.beta){
          beta.in[,i] <- rep(beta.point[i], n)
        }
      }
    }else{
    
    }

      for(i in 1:n) {
        if(mod[1] == TRUE){             ## set p vals
          model[['p']] <<- p.in[i]
        }
        if(mod[2] == TRUE){                ## set alpha vals
          model[['alpha']]<<- alpha.in[i,]
        }
        if(mod[3] == TRUE){                ## set beta vals
          model[['beta']]<<- beta.in[i,]
        }

        model$simulate(dependentNodes)
        sim[,i] <- model$y
      }

  
    returnType(double(2))
    return(sim)
  
  }
)


setup and compile code:
occ.model <- nimbleModel(code =  occ.betas.yrAsCov.beta0dm,
                        constants = const,
                        inits = list(
                          p = p.s,
                          beta = beta.in
                        )
)

c.occ.model<-compileNimble(occ.model)

nodes = c('p', 'beta')

simulate.model <- n.simulateModel.occ.dist(occ.model, nodes)
c.simulate.model <- compileNimble(simulate.model, showCompilerOutput = T)

error:
compiling... this may take a minute. On some systems there may be some compiler warnings that can be safely ignored.
Error in if (useMap & length(varAndIndices$indices) == 0) { :
  argument is of length zero

I can share the occupancy model, and inputs if needed for troubleshooting.
Thank you,

Brian

hi Brian,

I commented out the lines related to 'dependentNodes' so I could try to see what was going wrong without the complication of the actual model you are using.

When I do that, here's what I see. 

In the "if(mod[2] == TRUE){" block, you use 'beta.index' when I think you mean to use 'alpha.index'. 
When I run your code, I see a warning related to this:

In addition: Warning message:
variable 'beta.index' has not been created yet. 

I also get an error message that points out that you created 'sim' as an integer matrix but you then return 'sim' as the output and the returnType is double. So you need to make that consistent. 

Now it might be that you get a different error because in your case you have the lines related to 'dependentNodes'. But I don't see why those lines would cause a problem...

-chris

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: nimble function compile error (simulate model)
parts:
Hi Brian,

To follow up on this, yes you are correct that model[['alpha']] will cause a problem during compilation even if the condition to use that piece of code will not be satisfied in a particular use case.  The compiler attempts to partially evaluate uses of the model, which in this case means resolving 'alpha' within 'model' at compile-time.  One way to do what you want would be to turn mod from a run argument to a setup argument (so it won't change for a particular instance of the nimbleFunction), create alpha_name in the setup code, and use it as model[[alpha_name]] in the run code.  If you will be needing it, set alpha_name <- 'alpha'.  If not, set it to some other variable name in the model just so it can point to something valid.  (It is still not looked up dynamically by name at run-time, but doing it this way allows different instances of the nimbleFunction to have different values of alpha_name.)  Another solution would be to include a dummy node like `alpha[1:2] <- c(0,0)` in the model even when it is not needed, and then it will at least exist for the nimbleFunction.

HTH
-Perry

On Saturday, July 3, 2021 at 12:40:10 PM UTC-7 pdevalpine wrote:
Hi Brian,

To follow up on this, yes you are correct that model[['alpha']] will cause a problem during compilation even if the condition to use that piece of code will not be satisfied in a particular use case.  The compiler attempts to partially evaluate uses of the model, which in this case means resolving 'alpha' within 'model' at compile-time.  One way to do what you want would be to turn mod from a run argument to a setup argument (so it won't change for a particular instance of the nimbleFunction), create alpha_name in the setup code, and use it as model[[alpha_name]] in the run code.  If you will be needing it, set alpha_name <- 'alpha'.  If not, set it to some other variable name in the model just so it can point to something valid.  (It is still not looked up dynamically by name at run-time, but doing it this way allows different instances of the nimbleFunction to have different values of alpha_name.)  Another solution would be to include a dummy node like `alpha[1:2] <- c(0,0)` in the model even when it is not needed, and then it will at least exist for the nimbleFunction.

HTH
-Perry

-chris
